name: Iob
overview: Iob was a male member of the tribe of Issachar, known as the son of Issachar. He appears in the genealogical lists of Israel's sons who journeyed to Egypt, marking him as part of the foundational family groups that formed the nation of Israel. He is also identified with the Jashubites, a clan within Issachar.
namesAndTitles: The name Iob is presented without a given meaning in Scripture. He is also called Jashub, which means "he returns," highlighting a possible thematic connection to return or restoration within his lineage. Neither name is indicated as being divinely given.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Iob as the son of Issachar, establishing his direct paternal lineage. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are detailed for Iob in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Iob's significance lies in his place within the genealogy of Israel, specifically as a son of Issachar who journeyed to Egypt with Jacob's family. His identification with the Jashubites connects him to a distinct clan within the tribe of Issachar, contributing to the historical and tribal structure of Israel as it prepared for its future as a nation. This genealogical mention underscores God's providential preservation of His people through the patriarchal line.
